metadata.title: Whole-Cell Patch-Clamp Electrophysiology (gigaseal → break-in → voltage-clamp & current-clamp recording)
metadata.purpose: Establish the whole-cell patch-clamp configuration on a single neuron and record membrane currents (voltage clamp) and membrane potential / evoked action potentials (current clamp) using a defined instrument stimulus program.
metadata.scope: Manual whole-cell recording from cultured / iPSC-derived neurons using a K-gluconate internal solution. Covers pipette preparation, gigaseal formation, break-in, and a representative voltage-step (IV) family plus current-clamp recording. Out of scope: cell-attached / perforated / outside-out patch modes, dynamic clamp, and automated (planar) patch-clamp.
beforeYouBegin: Freshly prepare and filter internal and external solutions; verify pH and osmolarity before use.
Pull patch pipettes to a resistance of 3-7 MOhm and, if needed, fire-polish; keep dust-free.

This JSON encodes an instrument STIMULUS PROGRAM (holding potential, voltage-step family, sampling/filter), not a reagent-only workflow; acquisition parameters must be entered into the amplifier/acquisition software.
Liquid junction potential (LJP) for K-gluconate internal vs aCSF is not corrected here and must be measured/applied per your rig.

tables.title: External (bath) aCSF recipe
tables.note: ~310 mOsm/L; bubble with 95% O2 / 5% CO2. Source src1.

tables.title: Voltage-clamp step family (stimulus program / sweep loop)
rows: -70 mV for EPSCs; 0 mV for IPSCs (src1)
DERIVED = (50 mV span from -80 to +50)/5 + 1; verify against rig
tables.note: WORKAROUND: the schema has no native stimulus-program / sweep-loop construct, so the voltage-step family is encoded as a table. Values are representative and combined across sources; treat as needsReview and confirm against the target current under study.

steps.action: Back-fill a pulled borosilicate pipette with K-gluconate internal solution and mount on the headstage; measure pipette resistance in the bath.
steps.expectedResult: Stable pipette resistance of 3-7 MOhm with no clogging.
steps.criticalNotes: WORKAROUND: electrical resistance (MOhm) has no parameter.type in the enum, so type 'other' with unit MOhm is used.

steps.action: Place cells in the recording chamber and start continuous bath perfusion with oxygenated aCSF.
steps.expectedResult: Healthy cell identified; stable perfusion, no bubbles over the cell.
steps.criticalNotes: WORKAROUND: perfusion flow rate (mL/min) has no dedicated parameter.type; encoded as 'other'.

steps.action: Apply light positive pressure, lower the pipette onto the cell, then release the pressure to form a gigaseal; monitor with a repeated voltage test pulse.
steps.criticalNotes: WORKAROUND: seal resistance (GOhm) uses type 'other'. Test pulse combines a voltage (mV) and a repetition frequency (Hz) as two separate parameters because there is no single 'test-pulse' construct.

sourceReferences.excerpt: 10 mV test pulse at 100 Hz ... Release the positive pressure to obtain a GOhm seal ... 1 GOhm

steps.action: Rupture the patch to enter whole-cell mode using brief suction pulses or the amplifier 'zap' function; then monitor series (access) resistance.
steps.expectedResult: Whole-cell configuration achieved; capacitive transients appear; stable, low series resistance.
steps.criticalNotes: WORKAROUND: series/access resistance (MOhm) has no enum type -> 'other' with value null + needsReview because the source gives no target value for this cell type.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Apply light and short suction pulses ... or brief electrical pulses via zap function

steps.action: Configure the acquisition: set holding potential and the digitizer sampling rate and anti-alias filter.

parameters.rawText: -70 mV to record spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents
0 mV to record spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic currents
low-pass Bessel filter (set below Nyquist; fetched review example used -3 dB Gaussian at 50 Hz)

steps.expectedResult: Amplifier held at command potential; acquisition sampling and filter configured.
steps.criticalNotes: Sampling rate and filter cutoff are frequencies (kHz), which map cleanly to parameter.type 'frequency'. Holding potential maps to 'voltage'. Filter value left null with needsReview: the fetched source (src2) reports a 50 Hz Gaussian example, whereas 10 kHz Bessel is a common rig setting not verified in a single fetched source.

sourceReferences.excerpt: sampling frequency of 10 kHz; Lowpass filtered (Gaussian, -3 dB cutoff at 50 Hz)

steps.action: Run the voltage-step (IV) family: from the holding potential, apply command steps across the range in fixed increments, each held for the step duration, repeating every inter-sweep interval; acquire the current family.
steps.expectedResult: A family of voltage-dependent membrane currents; an IV relationship can be constructed.
steps.criticalNotes: WORKAROUND: the sweep-loop stimulus program is captured both as flat parameters here and as table t3, because the schema has no loop/sweep-family construct. The sweep count is a DERIVED value (schema has no computed-quantity field) placed in a 'count' parameter with needsReview.

sourceReferences.excerpt: +-5 mV, +-10 mV steps (50 ms); steps to +50/+60 mV

steps.action: Switch the amplifier to current-clamp; hold the cell near rest with a small bias current, then inject a family of depolarizing current steps to evoke action potentials.

parameters.rawText: inject depolarizing current steps (step size/range not specified in source)

steps.expectedResult: Resting membrane potential recorded; graded action-potential firing with increasing current injection.
steps.criticalNotes: Current-clamp injection step family (size, range, duration) is not specified in the sources -> current parameter value null + needsReview rather than fabricated.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Change to a negative voltage close to the expected cell resting potential (-60 to -70 mV)

steps.action: Save and analyze traces (e.g., in Clampfit); apply the liquid junction potential correction and report membrane properties.
steps.expectedResult: IV curves, input resistance, and firing properties reported.
steps.criticalNotes: Liquid junction potential (K-gluconate internal vs aCSF) is a computed correction with no native schema field; it is flagged here and in beforeYouBegin and must be measured/applied per rig.

controls.name: Gigaseal quality control
controls.description: Accept a cell only if seal resistance is >= 1 GOhm before break-in.

controls.name: Series-resistance monitoring
controls.description: Track series (access) resistance throughout; discard the recording if it drifts substantially.

controls.name: Pharmacological isolation control
controls.description: Optionally apply 20 uM TTX and/or 2 mM CoCl2 to confirm the identity of recorded currents (Na+ / Ca2+).

expectedOutputs: Gigaohm seal (>= 1 GOhm) followed by stable whole-cell access.
Voltage-clamp current family and derived current-voltage (IV) relationship.
Current-clamp resting membrane potential and evoked action-potential traces.
Digitized recording files with the stimulus program metadata.

troubleshooting.cause: Dirty pipette tip, unhealthy cell, or too much positive pressure
troubleshooting.solution: Use a fresh pipette, select a healthier cell, and reduce positive pressure before contact
Use gentler, briefer suction pulses or a shorter zap

troubleshooting.cause: Rising series resistance or dialysis of the cell
troubleshooting.solution: Monitor and compensate series resistance; limit recording duration

troubleshooting.cause: Filter cutoff or sampling rate set inappropriately
troubleshooting.solution: Set the low-pass filter below the Nyquist frequency and sample at >= 2x the filter cutoff

safety: TTX is a potent neurotoxin; CoCl2 is toxic - handle and dispose per institutional rules.
Follow institutional biosafety approval for the specific cell source (human iPSC-derived neurons).
limitations: The voltage-step family (range/increment/duration/interval/sweep count) and the current-clamp injection family are representative, combined across sources, and marked needsReview; they must be tailored to the current/cell under study. Filter cutoff, series-resistance target, temperature, and liquid junction potential are not fixed by the primary source. The schema has no native stimulus-program (sweep-loop) construct, so the program is expressed via a table plus flat parameters.
